board.title: AI chip factories are still dramatically under-built
board.story: The plants that make the chips were not built fast enough for the demand now hitting them. That shortage, not a China-invasion story, is still the brake. New tapes this week did not kill it. They keep running into the same wall.
board.force: they did not build enough plants. Supply and demand, not political theater.
board.from: the TSMC story already kept. Fed this week by All-In, Dylan Patel, Stratechery.

board.title: In July the market panicked. The factories did not.
board.story: AI stock prices had a crash month that felt like 2022. Gavin Baker went looking for a real-world reason and could not find one. Chips were getting easier to get, rental prices were up, memory was up, and people were using more tokens, not less. The scare was in the price of the shares. It was not in the plants.
board.force: the share price and the factory can point opposite ways. Read both.
board.from: Gavin Baker, Invest Like the Best, 4 Aug. MSM: FT Alphaville, BBC, and the FSB ran the July “AI bubble” scare.

board.title: Compute is getting dearer, and old cards still earn
board.story: Useful intelligence is getting more expensive, not cheaper. An H100 is worth more today than three years ago. When a model got ten times cheaper, people used it thirteen times more. A six-year write-off looks wrong because the cards stay in the money long after the accountant is done with them.
board.force: more demand for the same scarce machines, and the machines last.
board.from: the compute-dearer story already kept. Enforced this week by Atallah, Dylan Patel, Stratechery.

board.title: The money is going to the plants, not the next model
board.story: Google is putting cash into data-center plants, not into the next model. Inside the company the cloud team wants to rent those chips out, and the model team wants the same chips to train. The chips are winning.
board.force: capital follows the scarce physical thing (plants, power, chips), not the research team.
board.from: All-In 8 Aug (Friedberg, Gerstner). Stratechery: Google the capital company.

board.title: Ordinary funding may be exhausted. That is why they are lending to themselves.
board.story: The plants and the labs need more cash than earnings, banks, and ordinary borrowing can cover. That claim still needs proof. If it is true, they have to invent other money: chip sellers lending to their own buyers, Nvidia reaching into insurance and pension money, the same dollars going around the same few companies and getting counted as revenue. Circular funding and the debt pile are what you do when the normal tap is dry. The BIS has already said the biggest cloud companies are spending faster than they earn. That is a start, not a close.
board.force: if ordinary money is exhausted, the stack starts lending to itself. Prove the exhaustion, not the weirdness.
board.from: the board frame. All-In (Gurley circular). Stratechery 11 Aug Nvidia’s risky business. Gavin Baker on credit wrappers. BIS on hyperscaler spend vs cash.
board.note: Sits next to prediction P2. No fourth thesis minted this walk.

board.title: Power is the problem. Nobody agrees what happens next.
board.story: Everyone serious now says intelligence will hit a wall made of electricity. That part is shared. The fight is about the future. One camp says China will add far more power than America next year, so energy stays the limit. Another camp says you can build power, and the real 2030 bind is the rarest machines that make the chips. A third camp says put the plants in space, because on the ground you cannot get a permit. These cannot all be right about what happens next.
board.force: the problem is agreed. The path and the fix are not. The world will pick by what actually fails first.
board.from: Vishria 11 Aug. Dylan Patel 13 Mar. Dwarkesh Elon 5 Feb. Stratechery SpaceX IPO.

board.title: China is locking the ugly supply chains
board.story: China stopped exporting research monkeys. Prices jumped, US labs ran short. It already refines most rare earths and is moving to own the robots that run the mines, not just the rocks. In the Iran oil shock it quietly cut imports from stockpiles the West cannot see. The FCC just swept robot vacuums and humanoids onto a national-security import list. Each of these is an input the West did not build a second source for.
board.force: whoever owns the unglamorous input can turn it off.
board.from: ChinaTalk 14 Jul–13 Aug (monkeys, minerals, oil, FCC robots).

board.title: The payment system has not caught up to the model
board.story: Intelligence is getting expensive. The rails that pay for it are still yesterday’s rails. Stripe talks about software agents that need to pay for things. A payments founder says the banker in your pocket is coming and is not here. This is not a crypto-price story. It is that the model and the payment have not joined up.
board.force: the old money system has not caught up to who should pay, or how.
board.from: Founders 2 Aug Micky Malka. Stripe / Collison.

board.title: The chip factories will still be the bottleneck at Christmas, even if the stocks crash again
board.story: The plants that make AI chips were not built fast enough. That is why computers for intelligence are expensive, and why a three-year-old chip still earns money. In July the newspapers and the stock market had a panic. A fund manager went looking for a factory reason and could not find one. The scare was in the share price. It was not in the factories.
board.call: By 31 December 2026 that is still true. The wait for a new chip, and the price to rent one, will still be tight or tighter.
board.wrong_if: the wait gets easy and rents collapse, while everyone is still talking about AI.
board.note: Evidence for TH-01. Not a second thesis.

board.title: If ordinary money is exhausted, one of these alternative deals will break in public within a year
board.story: If the usual funding is exhausted, companies are no longer just paying cash. Chip sellers are lending to their own buyers. Nvidia is reaching into insurance money and pension money. The same dollars go around the same few companies and get counted as revenue. That can look like a boom on paper while the cash never came from a real customer.
board.call: Before 14 August 2027, one of these loans or insurance deals will blow up, get rewritten, or show up in a newspaper with a real company name on it. A podcast complaining about circular money is not enough.
board.wrong_if: a year from now the plants are still being paid with ordinary cash, and the strange paper is gone.
board.note: Sits next to board card 6. Not minted as a thesis this walk.

board.title: OpenAI and Anthropic will still take the money. Cheap models will take the usage.
board.story: There are two markets now, and they are not the same. The two best labs can still charge for the model itself. Everyone a year behind can only charge for computers and consulting. Cheap and Chinese open models already do most of the everyday work. Money and usage have split.
board.call: A year from now that split is still there. The expensive labs still collect most of the dollars. The cheap models still do most of the work.
board.wrong_if: a cheap model starts collecting the dollars too, or the expensive labs lose the dollar pile.
board.note: Priced / capture question. Not a new desk item.

board.title: China catching up in trailing-edge robotics semiconductors
board.story: More than 300 Chinese auto and industrial chip suppliers are on the trailing-edge nodes that robots actually use. NXP and Infineon share is fading in those sockets. This is not a leading-edge TSMC story.
board.force: the chips inside robots are older nodes, and China is filling that shelf.

board.title: Unitree G1 at $16K against a ~$100K Western humanoid
board.story: Unitree is selling a G1 near $16,000. Western humanoids are still talked about near $100,000. UBTech is targeting about 1,000 units. Price and shipment talk, not a proven Western displacement.
board.force: the cheap unit is already a product. The expensive unit is still a plan.

board.title: China holds about 90% of permanent magnets
board.story: China still refines and makes most of the permanent magnets a motor needs. A Made-in-USA label after substantial transformation does not create a second magnet mine.
board.force: the magnet is the input. Assembly is not a substitute.

theses_6_12.title: The plants are still the scarce thing, and July’s scare was in the shares
theses_6_12.claim: The factories that make the chips were not built fast enough for the demand now hitting them. That shortage is still the brake. In July the shares panicked and the factories did not: chips were getting easier to get, rental and memory prices were up, and token use was up. Capital is already moving toward the plants, not the next model. The 6–12 month picture is that the physical thing stays scarce, and that July was a price event, not a factory event.
theses_6_12.clock: 6–12 months. Call window overlaps P1 (bottleneck still true at Christmas).
theses_6_12.kill: utilization down, rental and memory prices down, large capex cancelled. A second share-price scare without those prints is not a kill.
theses_6_12.priced: Checked 14 Aug 2026 Yahoo last prints. Default plant names already assume a lot of the good case: TSM $426.35 is −10.7% from the 30 Jun high and +13.8% off the 29 Jul scare close; MU $971.66 is +240% YTD and +31.5% off the 29 Jul close $739. Power tape did not run with them in 2026 (VST −8.2% YTD, −32% from the Sep 2025 high). Physical still tight. Not a buy on the spent names.
theses_6_12.skew: The honest side is long the scarce physical thing. Equity names that everyone already uses for this view (the foundry, the obvious power names) may have no skew left. That is why this is live and not on the desk.
theses_6_12.desk: not on desk as a buy — plant tape spent; power is the less-spent vehicle and still a wait

theses_6_12.title: China already owns the ugly inputs Western robots need
theses_6_12.claim: China stopped the monkeys, holds the rare earths and about 90% of the permanent magnets, is filling the trailing-edge MCU sockets robots actually use, and is already shipping a cheap humanoid unit. The West did not build a second source for the unglamorous inputs. That is one situation: the input is already theirs. It is not a claim that a US-listed humanoid works, or that a Western robot company is the way to hold it.
theses_6_12.kill: magnet export relief plus a real Western second source, or Chinese humanoid shipments fail in public numbers.
theses_6_12.priced: Checked 14 Aug 2026. Chinese magnet landlords did not run this year (JL MAG 6680.HK HK$17.16, −7% YTD, −40% from the Oct 2025 high). The Western second-source names (MP, Lynas) are the kill side, not the hold.
theses_6_12.skew: The obvious long — a US-listed humanoid — is the expensive side of the same fact. The magnet landlord is now named (ST-03) and is a wait. Trailing-edge socket still unnamed.
theses_6_12.desk: not on desk as a buy — expression now written (CA-02); magnet name is a wait, trailing-edge socket still unnamed

theses_6_12.title: The model can spend. The payment rail cannot.
theses_6_12.claim: Intelligence is getting expensive. The rails that pay for it are still yesterday’s rails. Stripe talks about agents that need to pay. Malka’s point is that the banker in your pocket is coming and is not here. The model and the payment have not joined up. That is the situation. It is not a crypto-price story, and it is not a claim that a new payments winner already exists.
theses_6_12.kill: agents stay demos; existing rails (Visa, Stripe, banks) absorb the traffic without a new winner.
theses_6_12.priced: “AI payments” is an easy story and is probably in several names already. Not checked live.
theses_6_12.skew: On the obvious names this looks like 10%, not 10x, unless a cheap specific expression appears. That is a failed skew gate, not a dead picture.
theses_6_12.desk: failed skew gate — not enough asymmetry on the obvious names

thesis_candidates.title: Plant-and-power landlords
thesis_candidates.object: An expression of TH-01, not a stock, not a buy. Sit with whoever owns the scarce physical thing — the foundry, the memory plants, the power landlords. This pass named the vehicles and screened them. None of them are a buy.
thesis_candidates.what_it_is: A thesis candidate. The shape of how TH-01 would be held.
thesis_candidates.what_it_is_not: A stock. A buy. A ticker. The next model. A spender. A tool-maker or a test-side consumable.
thesis_candidates.why_unfinished: The hold is written. The names are screened. Sit remains the desk answer because plant tape is spent and power still waits on both conditions.
thesis_candidates.clock_kill: The plants that make the leading chips, and the electricity that turns them on, stay scarce. Utilization stays high. Memory prices and GPU rents do not collapse. Big build programs at foundries / memory / power queue are not cancelled. A second scare in the shares, by itself, is not a kill.
thesis_candidates.world_state: confirmed on the physical; spent on the default plant names; fade/wait on power
thesis_candidates.note: ST-01, ST-02, and ST-08 are one factor. Power is the less-spent tape. Do not treat three monitors as three bets.
thesis_candidates.tape: 14 Aug 2026 Yahoo lasts. Physical agreeing: DigiTimes (mid-Aug) says 2027 DRAM/HBM from the three memory plants is booked; Micron 12 Aug said 2027 tighter than 2026 and DRAM is the constraint, not power. Plant tape spent: TSM $426.35 is +40% YTD and already bought back the July scare; MU $971.66 is +240% YTD and +31.5% off 29 Jul $739. Power tape did not run with them: VST $148.13 is −8.2% YTD and −32% from 22 Sep 2025 $217.92. Texas pause (Abbott 3 Aug, ERCOT Batch Zero delayed, PUCT 20 Aug) is a queue audit, not a print that the landlord already gets paid. Sit.
thesis_candidates.how_the_hold_fails: Even if TH-01 is true, the plant can stay scarce and the landlord still not get paid (customer keeps the surplus; memory contracts already locked the rent; the Texas queue is mostly phantom — Vistra’s own CEO said 8 Aug he wants the queue culled). Power load that is real is a 2027–28 hookup. That is late for a 6–12 month clock.
thesis_candidates.desk: Sit. Hang is real. Plant names spent. Power is a wait, not an action.

thesis_candidates.title: Ugly-input landlords
thesis_candidates.object: Expression of TH-02. Sit with whoever already owns the magnet. Not a US-listed humanoid. Not a Western rare-earth second source — that is the kill, so MP and Lynas die if thrown as longs.
thesis_candidates.what_it_is: Input / squeeze side of TH-02. Magnet vehicle is now named (ST-03). Trailing-edge socket is still unnamed.
thesis_candidates.what_it_is_not: A US humanoid. A Western mine or magnet second source. A fabless MCU with a robot slide.
thesis_candidates.why_unfinished: Magnet name is screened and waiting. Trailing-edge socket: GigaDevice is fabless plus a product story, not a verified robot socket we can stand behind. Hua Hong / SMIC is a China-foundry factor this desk does not understand well enough this pass. Too hard is a legal disposition.
thesis_candidates.clock_kill: inherits TH-02 — magnet export relief plus a real Western second source, or Chinese humanoid shipments fail in public numbers.
thesis_candidates.tape: 14 Aug 2026. China still makes most of the permanent magnets a motor needs. JL MAG 6680.HK HK$17.16, −7% YTD, −40% from 13 Oct 2025. The tape of the landlord is not running. MP $58.74 bounced +42% off its 29 Jul low — that is the kill-side name catching a bid, not our hold.
thesis_candidates.how_the_hold_fails: Even if China still owns the magnet, the listed landlord can be an EV-cycle stock (JL MAG’s FY2025 magnet revenue was mostly NEV, robot rotors still small-batch). Export licences can sit with the state, not the shareholder. A Made-in-USA label after substantial transformation is not a second mine, but a real Western magnet plant would be the kill.
thesis_candidates.desk: Magnet vehicle written. Socket unnamed. Sit. Not a buy.

screen.title: Taiwan Semiconductor (TSM) — hang is real, skew is not
screen.object: The default foundry name for CA-01. Honest vehicle for the scarce plant. Already the name everyone uses. Not a buy at this tape.
screen.hang: TH-01 / CA-01. They own the leading-edge plants. Customer cannot leave that node for a long time. This is a franchise, and the asking price already assumes a lot of the good case.
screen.how_it_makes_money: Customers pay to have leading-edge chips made in plants almost nobody else can copy. That is the scarce slot.
screen.invert: The good case is the default Wall Street hold. A true bottleneck can still leave no unused skew. One customer set (AI accelerators) can keep the surplus. Geopolitics is a company risk, not the TH-01 kill.
screen.world_state: confirmed physical, spent on this name
screen.priced: 14 Aug 2026 Yahoo last $426.35. +40.3% YTD from 31 Dec 2025 $303.89. 30 Jun $477.57 (the 52-week high in this window). 29 Jul scare close $374.67. Now +13.8% off that close and only −10.7% from the high. July was a wiggle, already bought back.
screen.downside: Retest of 29 Jul $374.67 is about 12% from $426. A real TH-01 kill is larger than that. Do not write 10x down.
screen.upside: Back to $477.57 is about 12%. Residual if P1 holds to Christmas. Also what the default foundry holder already owns.
screen.clock: TH-01 6–12 months, overlaps P1 (bottleneck still true at Christmas).
screen.kill: Inherited: utilization down, rental and memory prices down, large capex cancelled. None have printed.
screen.other_vehicle: Same factor as ST-02 and ST-08. Power is the less-spent tape. Memory (MU) bounced harder. Sitting is the other use of the same capital.
screen.disposition: MONITOR via WL-01. Hang is real. Skew is not, after the July scare was bought back.
screen.desk: Not a buy. Wait for both conditions.

screen.title: Vistra (VST) — power landlord, clocks do not match
screen.object: The named power vehicle for CA-01. Texas merchant generator plus a 20-year 1.2 GW Comanche Peak PPA with Amazon from 2027. Closest US equity to ‘owns the electrons.’ CEG, NRG, and TLN are the same factor — do not stack them.
screen.hang: TH-01 / CA-01, power side. They already own plants on ERCOT. The Texas large-load queue is the physical tell. Not a turbine vendor (GEV) and not a cooling vendor (VRT).
screen.how_it_makes_money: They make electricity and sell it, retail and wholesale, and they hedge. The Amazon nuclear PPA is the piece a hyperscaler cannot easily leave once hooked. The rest is a commodity cycle with a hedge book.
screen.invert: CEO James Burke, 8 Aug earnings: 2026 ERCOT wholesale is soft, data-center hookup is 2027–28, and he wants the 474 GW queue culled. That is CA-01’s phantom-queue failure, said out loud. The Amazon PPA was announced 29 Sep 2025 during the run to $217.92. Load-growth talk was cut to 4–6% from 5–6%. PJM price-cap talk. This is a cycle plus one dated PPA, not a foundry franchise. Clock mismatch: TH-01 is a 6–12 month chip-plant bet; Vistra’s data-center load is a 2027–28 hookup.
screen.world_state: physical queue is real and also phantom; name tape is a 2026 fade after a 2025 AI-power run
screen.priced: 14 Aug 2026 Yahoo last $148.13. −8.2% YTD from 31 Dec 2025 $161.33. 22 Sep 2025 high $217.92 (−32%). 19 May 2026 low $134.71. 29 Jul $142.81, now +3.7%. About $55B cap on mid-Aug 2026 reads. Q2 2026 ongoing adj. EBITDA $1.767B; 2026 guide $6.8–7.6B reaffirmed. Back to $217.92 is about +47%. Not desk skew.
screen.downside: Retest of 19 May $134.71 is about 9% from $148. Further if 2027 ERCOT forwards stay below their midpoint opportunity. Do not write 10x down — integrated retail plus hedges.
screen.upside: Old high $217.92 is +47%. That is a 2025 story getting re-rated, not unused TH-01 skew. Street already used Vistra as the default AI-power name last year.
screen.clock: Company clock is 2027–28 hookup and the PUCT 20 Aug good-cause meeting on Batch Zero. TH-01’s Christmas bottleneck does not transfer cleanly onto 2027 load.
screen.kill: Do not inherit the chip-plant kill onto a generator without a sentence. This name dies if contracted data-center load slips, ERCOT stays soft into the PPA start, or the queue audit shows the 474 GW was mostly phantom and nothing real replaces it. A second semi scare without those prints is not this name’s kill.
screen.other_vehicle: CEG / NRG / TLN are the same factor. TSM and MU are the plant side of the same theme, already spent. Sit is the other use of the capital.
screen.disposition: MONITOR via WL-03. Hang is the best power join. Skew is not. Clocks do not match. Not Action.
screen.desk: Not a buy. Same shape as the other waits: both conditions, or nothing.

screen.title: JL MAG (6680.HK) — magnet landlord, still an EV cycle
screen.object: The named magnet vehicle for CA-02. Dual-listed 300748.SZ / 6680.HK. They make the NdFeB magnets a motor needs. Not a US humanoid. Not MP. Northern Rare Earth 600111.SS is upstream of the same chain (A-share only this pass).
